notes.title: Let It Cook
notes.content:
Hello Goblin Gang! Happy February. There's been pretty steady interest in WOFG! through January, and demo playtimes keep going up. This is very encouraging for us. Thanks to everyone who is playing our little goblin game. 

I know it's been a while since our last update, and unfortunately this one is also very small. 

[u][b]In this Update:[/b][/u]
[list]
[*] Small settings tweaks and changes.
[*] New gravity handling which should fix the "floating" bug when Goblins walk over small ledges.
[/list]
That's it. Sorry if you were hoping for more.  

That's the bad news but I've got good news too! WOFG! has a bright future. We've been making slow but steady progress rebuilding the goblin controller from the ground up. What's in the demo now is fun- but it's also not quite right. This rebuild will give us a chance to revisit some mechanics we didn't quite get right and improve a lot of the code that's affecting the game's performance. 

[u][b]What are the goals of the Goblin rebuild?[/b][/u]
[list]
[*][b]Better Sprinting[/b]- we want the Gobs to be able to hit ramps and get big air, and drift around corners. It's no secret WOFG! is heavily inspired by the ragdoll physics in sports games like Pro Skater and Descenders. If the Goblins go faster then they crash harder, that's just good fun.
[*][b]More Animations[/b] - More animations make our ragdoll better. We want to add animations for sliding, changing directions, punch combos, long-jumps, and more.
[*][b]Better Jumping[/b] - Standard jumping in the demo is alright, but wall jumps, sprint jumps, and hanging jumps are janky. True Goblin parkour needs good jumps.  
[*][b] Ability to Climb [/b]- Your Gob should be able to grab stuff and pull themselves up. It's something we've wanted for a while- and you actually can do it in the demo right now. It's just not easy or intuitive. If you could easily climb stuff with the existing grab mechanics it would open up all kinds of interesting platforming.   
[*][b]Items[/b]- We've always wanted to have items that change the way the Goblin's attacks work. We've prototyped this before but we cut it from the demo because it wasn't quite ready. This reworks gives us a chance to build a flexible item system so we can easily add new items as we continue development. 
[*][b]Better Goblin Buddies [/b]- At the same time as rebuilding the player's Goblins we are rebuilding the NPC Goblins too. We are aiming for better pathfinding and decision making. Again we want to build in a way that will let us easily add new behaviors. 
[*][b]Performance[/b] - We want WOFG! to run better on more hardware. We've already been able to streamline a lot of the code that's running the demo and test builds have been encouraging.  
[/list]

So that's what we are working on. We want to take the time to get this right- and it's going to take as long as it takes. If we can build a solid base now we will be able to make a better game long-term. Stay tuned, and let it cook. These Goblins are going to be great!

Finally, Steam's Couch is happening right now! I'm not sure how big a deal it is, but WOFG! is registered to participate. Maybe this is a good time to grab a pal and take another hike up The Skrimble Thimble? 

As always, until next time, Watch Out for Goblins!

notes.title: Holiday Haymaker Update
notes.content:
Merry Christmas Goblin Gang! Or happy whatever winter holiday you celebrate! 
We’ve been diligently reworking our character controller and optimizing Watch Out for Goblins! so it runs more smoothly on more hardware. This is a pretty big rework and it’s going to take us some time, but we think it will absolutely be worth it. 

In the meantime, we’ve added a bit of winter weather to the Skrimble Isles and warped it up nice with new combat animations. It’s a small update, but it’s a good update.

[h2]So what’s new in WOFG! The Demo!?[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Big Bold Combat Animations[/b] - Our first run at combat animations was timid. We wanted snappy controls so we stayed away from anticipation frames, but this left the goblins with weak little punches that hardly looked like punches. No more of that! Our new punches have a ton of windup. The Gob’s now step in with wild haymakers that put their whole body into the punch. It feels so much better. Shove and uppercut animations have a similar glow up. 
[*] [b]More Goblin Stabilization [/b]- We’ve got another sackful of tweaks and changes that all have the goal of reducing the “scrambling” that happens when the goblins take a big hit. Scrambling is much reduced in this build- but it’s still there. We are going to keep trying to reduce it but it’s a struggle Unity’s physics engine has when chains of joints experience extreme forces. Dedicated Goblins will probably always be able to find a way to scramble if that’s the kind of thing you are into.      
[*] [b]Christmas Cosmetic[/b] - A fun new piece of goblin garb to collect. Jolly good fun.  
[/list]

[h2]What are we working on over the next month?[/h2]
[list]
[*][b] A Short Holiday Break [/b]- At least next week, we are going to work on not working on WOFG! We are going to spend Christmas and new years with our friends and families. Don’t worry, we will be back to dev in 2025.
[*] [b]Building a Great Goblin [/b]-  We have a good goblin. We want a Great Goblin. This is going to take some time. Over the last month we’ve been skill building and planning out everything we want the new goblin to be able to do. Early work is moving in a promising direction. If you want more details (maybe too many details) you can check our dev blog here: [url=https://sqyd.studio/dev-blog/]https://sqyd.studio/dev-blog/[/url]
[/list]

We plan to keep bringing improvements to the WOFG! The Demo! when they are ready. As always, thank you to everyone playing the demo and giving us your honest feedback. It only helps us keep making the game better.   

We will be back early in 2025 with another development update. Over the holidays- remember to watch out for goblins wherever you go. I think they like to roll around in dirty snowbanks.

notes.title: State of Dev November 2024
notes.content:
Hello Goblin Gang! Watch Out for Goblins! The Demo! has been live on Steam for about a month now. We have been watching people play, listening to feedback, and thinking about our next steps. Before I get into our development plans, thank you all for playing and sharing your experience with the demo. Seeing the big playtimes in our Steam stats gives us confidence that we are on the right track. 

So what next? It seems that there is still some friction in our character controller. Game performance also isn’t as good as we’d like it to be especially on the Steam deck and older PCs. The path forward is clear– it's time to refactor. This means taking some time to go back to the basics of the project, looking to enhance what is working and fix what isn’t. We now feel we have a pretty good idea of what Watch Out for Goblins! wants to be as a game. Now the task is to rebuild the foundation into something that is stable and easy to expend, without sacrificing any of the wacky ragdoll action that’s at the core of WOFG!
[h3]
Here’s what we plan to work on over the next month or so:[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]Character controller optimization.[/b] We love our character controller for a lot of things, but think it’s fair to say that it has some weird behavior that breaks the flow of the game. Sometimes the goblin is a little too stiff when they take a big hit, sometimes a mysterious force pulls the goblin off the cliff you’ve worked hard to climb. These problems can be very frustrating. The good news is that we think we can fix them, it’s just going to take a bit of an overhaul of some of the core goblin systems. 
[*] [b]Development tools.[/b] Now that we have a good idea of what a complete WOFG! will be, we are going to spend some time building custom development tools to help us create levels, mechanisms, and NPC behaviors quickly and easily. 
[*] [b]More models. [/b]This game needs some crazy creatures, super set pieces, and more bits of groady goblin garb to collect. We are going to spend some time toiling away in the Blender mines to make sure, when we have our character reworked and our dev tools in place, that we are ready to pack the game full of gooey Goblin content!
[/list]

Thanks again for following along as we continue to build our little goblin game. If you want more technical (and overwritten, personal, and possibly navel-gazing) updates on dev progress please check in on the [url=https://sqyd.studio/2024/11/12/refactoring-gobland-2-a-clean-project-with-unity-6/]SQYD.studio Dev Blog[/url]. If not, we will be back with another Steam Community Sate of Dev report next month. 

Until next time, please remember to Watch Out for Goblins! wherever you go. I hear they like to hide under piles of fallen leaves.

notes.title: WOFG! The Demo! - SPOOKY UPDATE
notes.content:
Watch Out for Goblins! The Demo! has been out for about two weeks now. Seeing people play the demo we made has been both exciting and terrifying. We’ve been learning a lot, listening to feedback, and thinking about how to incorporate it into the game. In the next few weeks we are taking some time to figure out our plans for the future. We have so many ideas on how to improve and expand our little goblin game. I expect we will have news to share soon. If you want to stay in the loop make sure you “Follow” Watch Out for Goblins! on Steam or on our website: [url=https://sqyd.studio/]SQYD.studio[/url]

One thing we did learn, judging from playtimes, some of you really seem to be having a lot of fun with the demo. For you, here’s a small Halloween themed update as a thank you. We hope you keep following our progress as Watch Out for Goblins! continues to grow.

[h3]What’s included in the SPOOKY UPDATE:[/h3]

[list]
[*] A very small, but very [i]spooky[/i] new level. Made with set pieces we couldn’t quite fit onto the Skrimble Iles.
[*][i] Chilling[/i] reskins for smashable pots and mud balls.
[*] Three pieces of [i]haunted[/i] new goblin garb to collect.
[*] A [i]terrifying[/i] grab bag of bug fixes and settings tweeks.
[*] A [i]creepy[/i] new goblin song- be careful, it’s an earworm.
[*] BALLOONS!
[/list]

We hope you have fun with this small update. Please follow along with development and please let us know what you think of the demo. Game design is iterative and we can only improve with your help.

Finally, as always, remember to watch out for goblins wherever you go. I hear there are a lot of them out and about this time of year. 

Happy Halloween!

notes.title: "Watch Out for Goblins! The Demo!" is Out Now!
notes.content:
Hello Goblin Gang. We are happy to announce that “Watch Out for Goblins! The Demo!” is now available to play. We are very proud of the demo and are excited to connect with new players. Playtesting and feedback has already shaped WOFG! immensely- and with a demo out in the wild we hope that you can keep helping us as we continue to develop our wacky goblin game. 

Aren't convinced you should try it out? Want a better idea of what the demo includes? I got you:

[list]
[*] Ability to run, jump, grab, and shove with an active ragdoll goblin.
[*] One map packed with stuff to explore- Welcome to the Skrimble Iles!
[*] Five silly NPC goblins to chat with and/or beat the snot out of.
[*] Eight Energy Widgets to activate and clear the mysterious sludge fog.
[*] Sixteen shiny Power Cogs to collect.
[*] Thirteen bit of goblin garb to grab- dress your Goblin to suit your style.
[*] Ten types of goblin mechanism to activate using the power of perpetual motion.
[*] Stuff to smash, platforming challenges, nooks to explore, mud, and more.
[*] Best part- play it all with a pal in splitscreen multiplayer.
[/list] 

Please check it out, share it with your friends, and let us know what you think. Here are some of the ways you can reach us:

[list]
[*][url=https://sqyd.studio/]On our website: SQYD.studio[/url]
[*][url=https://discord.gg/a5GtRbtnUe] Join our super chill discord server[/url]
[*][url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2887920/discussions/]Here on the Steam Community discussion boards [/url]  
[/list]

Thanks for reading to the end. I hope you play it and I hope you have some fun.
Until next time, please remember: Watch Out for Goblins!

notes.title: State of Dev September 2024
notes.content:
Happy September Goblin Gang! NextFest looms, and we’ve been hard at work preparing the  WOFG! demo. In fact, our demo build is now in our open playtest. If you want to help us polish it up by trying it out and giving us your honest feedback it would be greatly appreciated. You can sign up for the open playtest on the store page. If you’d rather wait until it’s out, you won’t have to wait long. We are planning to release the demo in early October. 

If you’d like to know what we’ve been working on for the past month and a bit, read on for this month’s State of Dev report:

[h2]Milestones Reached in the Last Month[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Level Design - [/b]The WOFG! demo will be set on the Skrimble Iles. We’ve been shaping the level to try to find a balance between guided progression and open exploration. We think we’ve managed that.
[*] [b]Goblin NPCs -[/b] We’ve created a “quest line” system for our NPC goblins that lets them change behaviors/dialogue based on things the players do on the map. We feel it gives the goblins a lot more personality and we are excited to expand on this system in the future.
[*] [b]Mechanisms! -[/b] We have a lot of things to collect, but we had nothing to spend them on. Mechanisms are our solution. Now you can place a Power Cog into an Energy Widget, which will activate any attached mechanisms. Some mechanisms (like the vending machines) are activated by spending your hard earned mud and bolts. We like the idea of slowly bringing life to Gobland as you explore and are happy with how the mechanisms system supports this. 
[/list]

[h2]Dev Goals for September[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Get Ready for Next Fest - [/b]The WOFG! demo is going to be in Steam’s October NextFest! The goal now is to focus all our effort on making the demo as polished and ready as it possibly can be. As I said above: we are currently running an open playtest of the demo content through Steam. We will be running this palytest until the end of September. Any feedback helps us learn what is working and what isn’t. Playtesting is what makes games good.
[/list]

That’s all for now. I’d better get back to it. Exciting times. Thanks for reading all the way to the end, you always impress me when you do. We will see you in the playtest if you want to help (you can find it on our store page). Otherwise, we hope you are excited to play the WOFG! Demo during NextFest next month. As always, until next time, remember - Watch Out for Goblins!

notes.title: State of Dev August 2024
notes.content:
Hi everybody! Time flies. It has been over a month since our last dev update but that doesn't mean we haven’t been hard at work. Here’s what’s been going on in Gobland over the past thirty plus days.
    
[h2]Milestones reached in the last month[/h2]
[list]
[*][b] Input prompts[/b] - We’ve got a system for proper input prompts. While we still recommend a gamepad, hopefully this will help keyboard and mouse players learn how to be a goblin. 
[*][b] Rebindable controls [/b]- We implemented a system to rebind gameplay controls. This will help people customize the controls the way they want, especially on mouse and keyboard- where player preferences are king. 
[*][b] Goblin customization[/b] - We added a bunch of cosmetic/customization options for the goblins. We have a fair number of clothing options already, and have plans for many more. For some reason goblins wearing sunglasses are very funny to me. 
[*] [b]Quick respawn[/b] -  By opening the fancy new goblin menu (press select), you can quickly respawn at any checkpoint you’ve previously activated.
[*] [b]New goblin verbs[/b] -  Goblins now have hand IK that helps them grab nearby objects. This especially helps them catch objects when in the air. When carrying something while airborne, jumping again spikes the object into the ground. It’s fun!
[/list]
[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2973890/view/4340992597630847693?l=english]All these features and more are live on our public playtest.[/url] Oh yeah! We have a public playtest. [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2887920/Watch_Out_For_Goblins/]You can sign up from the WOFG! store page.[/url] If you’d like to help us by providing feedback as we continue development we’d greatly appreciate the support. 

So what’s the plan for the next month of dev?

[h2]Dev goals for August[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Level design[/b] - This is our main focus for the month, we want to fill out a level with lots of wacky physics set pieces, loads of collectables to discover, quirky goblin NPCs to interact with, and at least a few tricky platforming challenges. 
[*][b] Climbing [/b]- We love how the goblins can grab and hang from platforms, but they need to be able to pull themselves up. We need to get some new animations implemented, but we are excited to see goblins climbing all over the scenery. 
[*] [b]Spend that mud [/b]- The aim is to let goblins spend their mud/other collectables to do cool stuff like: new cosmetics, more levels, to respawn items in the scene, and more. This is the big part of the game loop that’s missing- and once it’s in we think people will have a lot of good reasons to explore.
[/list]

Thank you all for your interest in our goblin game. We are coming into the homestretch towards our demo build, and we couldn’t be happier with how it’s progressing. There’s still a lot more to do–  so I better get to it. Until next time. Always, always: Watch Out for Goblins!

notes.title: State of Dev July 2024
notes.content:
First off, we are happy to announce that Watch Out For Goblins! will be participating in Steam’s October Next Fest which runs Oct 14th - 21st. This is very exciting for us. It also sets some hard deadlines for when we need to have a complete demo. So that’s what we are working on now: a cool demo. 
Read on to learn more about what we have been working on and what we will be working on this summer.  

[h1]State of Dev Report[/h1]

[h2]Dev milestones in the last month[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Smoothed out and squashed bugs in our character controller.[/b] Feeling pretty good now, though we will be continuing to tweak settings here and there. 
[*] [b]Setup a basic system for NPC behaviors. [/b]This will let us add quirky goblins to the world, set them up with lines of dialogue, and let them change behaviors based on milestones the players achieve.
[*] [b]Reworked the sprint system. [/b]Now you hold the button to boost your sprint speed and the sprint continues as long as the goblin has enough forward momentum.  
[*] [b]Started a new map. [/b]“The Skrimble Isles” are a smaller chain of islands which will eventually become our demo level.
[*] [b]Prototyped our first non-goblin NPCs.[/b] These are big flies that buzz about and try to headbutt nearby goblins.  
[*] [b]Overall game juice.[/b] This includes a bunch of new particles, sound effects, and textures.
[/list]

[h2]Dev goals in the next month[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]More love for keyboard and mouse players. [/b]Although we are designing the game to be played with a controller we want to support keyboard and mouse controls too. We will be working on a system to add dynamic button prompts and implementing control rebinding.
[*] [b]Create a player sub-menu.[/b] We want a menu that can: track collections (cogs, pages, cosmetics, etc.); allow players to customize their goblin’s name, voice, skin tone, and loincloth colour; and let players respawn at any checkpoint on the map that’s already been activated. 
[*] [b]Adding new animations.[/b] The new goblin voices have added a lot of character to our NPCs. We want more. Top priority are death and respawning animations for when the goblins drown in sludge. A goblin “explaining” animation for when the NPCs talk to you would be nice too.
[*] [b]Re-implementing IK.[/b] The goblins should look at interesting nearby things. We have a system for “look at” IK from very early in the project, just need to clean it up and re-enable it.
[*] [b]More explosions and breakable structures.[/b] Goblins need more fun stuff to smash! We also have these red barrels that don’t blow up- which I’m pretty sure is against video game law…
[*] [b]Prototype more features for the character controller.[/b] There are still a few more things we want to try- just to see if they are fun. I’ll tell you about them if they work out.
[/list]

[h2]The Playtest[/h2] 
Did you know? Watch Out For Goblins! [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2973890/view/4245287299526451665]has an open playtest, and it just got a major update[/url].  We’ve been posting our “in development” builds on Steam and collecting feedback on bugs and game mechanics. If you'd like to help us out and get involved as the game grows [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2887920/Watch_Out_For_Goblins/]head over to our store page and click “Join Playtest”.[/url] There’s already plenty of fun to be had with 1 - 4 players in split screen multiplayer. Please keep in mind that we are planning to close the playtest when the demo is ready.

Early feedback has already helped us learn what players are connecting with which lets us focus our dev time on what’s most important. We are regularly checking [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2973890]the steam community discussion board for your notes.[/url] If you’d like to chat with us devs directly we have a [url=https://discord.gg/a5GtRbtnUe]humble discord server where we are always happy to talk goblins.[/url]

If you’ve already played, thank you very much for your feedback and support. It means a lot to see people responding to our game. :)  

Wow. Are you still reading this? Cool. I like WOFG! as well. I’m all done with the announcement though. Until next time: Watch Out for Goblins!

notes.title: WOFG! Playtest is Live on Steam
notes.content:
The time has come to start sharing Watch Out for Goblins! with the world. We are looking for players interested in helping us playtest in advance of our early access release. If that sounds like something you want to help with you can now sign up for the WOFG! Playtest from our store page. 


[b]You can sign up to be a playtester right now, but first here are some things to keep in mind:[/b]
[list]
[*] The playtest will be time limited. This means you will eventually lose access to the playtest build. We plan to run the playtest for several months before replacing it with a publicly accessible demo version of WOFG!
[*] Save data is not guaranteed to carry over between playtest versions. You might lose all your progress (but that’s okay because the current game is very sand-boxy, there’s not much progress to make). 
[*] You may run into performance issues. We are trying to strike a balance between big open levels with lots of things to interact with and maintaining a consistent framerate. We’ve done some optimization on this build, and we have plans for more, but you should be aware that the game may not run well, especially on older hardware.
[*] You will encounter some bugs. We think we’ve squished the most game breaking ones, but there are likely still some lurking here and there. We are hoping that playtesters can help us find and squish more bugs before we launch the game properly.  
[/list]

With these warnings in mind you should head over to the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2887920/Watch_Out_For_Goblins/]Watch Out for Goblins! store page[/url] and sign up for the playtest. 

[b]But what can you do in the Watch Out for Goblins! playtest? [/b]
[list]
[*] Be a Goblin! Walk, run, jump, grab, punch, shove, and kick. All using an active ragdoll character blended with motion capture animations. 
[*] Explore a sandbox level to collect over thirty power cogs. 
[*] Interact with dozens of obstacles and contraptions for wacky physics interactions.
[*] Discover minigames: Smash yourself into obstacles to rack up points in a Goblin Ordeal, race through the checkpoints in a Goblin Footrace, and challenge your friends to competition with a rousing game of Goblin Sacker.
[*] Meet aggressive goblin NPCs that chase you down and give you a shove.   
[*] Drown in some sludge, knock yourself out with a barrel, fall off a mountain and land head first in a pile of dirt, and do it all with 1-4 players in split screen multiplayer.  
[/list]

If you made it this far, thanks for reading. :) We are very excited to start collecting feedback about the game we’ve been working on. I hope you consider joining the playtest. If you do, I hope you enjoy playing this early version of WOFG! I hope it makes you laugh. Most of all I hope you share your feedback with us so we can continue to improve the game as we work towards an early access release. 

We will keep our eyes on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/2973890]Steam Community page for the playtest [/url]for any feedback posted there. We also [url=https://discord.gg/a5GtRbtnUe]have a humble discord server[/url] where you can chat with us (the developers) directly. 

Thanks again for reading all the way to the end. For now, there’s nothing more to say except this: wherever you go and whatever you do, always, always, Watch Out For Goblins!
